footnotes.50: So St. Basil, as quoted below. “The husbandman having reaped the ear, seeks not again the seed under the root. But thou having the fruits, still givest not up that of which they grew. Thou plantest without land, thou reapest without seed.”
footnotes.51: St. Basil, Hom. in Ps. 14 (15), c. 3. “Interest upon interest, a bad offspring of bad parents. These may be well called a generation of vipers, I mean what our usuries bring forth. Vipers, they say, are yeaned, eating through their mother’s womb: and these usurious gains devour the debtors’ houses, and so have their birth.”
footnotes.52: There is here and afterwards a play upon the word τκο, gain, as a derivative of τκτειν, to bring forth, which can hardly be expressed in English.
